response_change.parent_relation: The target rate depends only on substrate through a fixed Michaelis-Menten saturation, so along the closed-vessel trajectory dP_dt is a single decreasing function of S with no direct dependence on accumulated product.
response_change.child_relation: The target rate depends on both remaining substrate and accumulated product because accumulated product competitively inhibits the enzyme, bending the rate decline more strongly as P rises even at the same S range reached later in the trajectory.
response_change.observable_effect: Compared with the parent, product formation slows disproportionately at later times when product has accumulated; early-time rates remain near the parent law while late-time rates are lower than any single fixed Michaelis-Menten curve fit can match across the full trajectory.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when product accumulates to a non-negligible fraction of the substrate-affinity scale, i.e. P comparable to the inhibition scale and not restricted to the very early low-conversion regime; with the given closed-vessel initial conditions this occurs naturally at intermediate to late times.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the mechanism already appears as a steeper-than-parent late-trajectory slowdown under the same initial-condition protocol; in holdout, the same product-dependent curvature extends to longer observation windows or parameter settings with stronger inhibition.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the zero-product-inhibition limit, e.g. inhibition constant taken to infinity so accumulated product no longer alters the rate.
plan.gap_statement: The current model treats the reaction environment as unaffected by its own product accumulation, omitting product inhibition that is common for soluble enzymes in closed assays.
plan.baseline_assumption: Relax the assumption that the conversion remains effectively described by a fixed irreversible Michaelis-Menten law independent of accumulated product throughout the observation window.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Competitive product inhibition, where product binds the enzyme and increases the apparent substrate affinity scale without violating nonnegativity or closed-vessel material conservation.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to let accumulated product feed back on the catalytic rate through product inhibition. The parent target mapping is shortcut by a fixed environment: once S is known, dP_dt is fully determined by one static saturation curve. In the child, dP_dt becomes a joint function of S and P, so the same remaining substrate level can correspond to a lower rate later in the run after more product has accumulated. The varied condition is progression along the observed closed-vessel trajectory, which changes P while conserving S+P; enzyme amount and solution conditions remain fixed. The concrete contrast is that early times with P near zero follow nearly the parent slope, but later times show extra downward curvature in dP_dt versus time or versus depletion progress because P suppresses turnover. This is scientifically admissible when product reaches an appreciable inhibitory scale; if inhibition is weak over the observed range, the effect may be hard to distinguish, and the parent is recovered smoothly in that limit. A single refitted parent parameter set cannot reproduce the specific early-near-parent and late-extra-slow pattern when it arises from direct dependence on accumulated P rather than from S depletion alone.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when the run samples appreciable conversion so that P becomes comparable to K_i and product accumulation is not negligible relative to the substrate/product concentration scale; the contrast is weakest when P << K_i throughout the observation window.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate conversion already shows mild extra late-time bending of dP_dt versus (S,P); in holdout trajectories extending to higher conversion, the same mechanism amplifies that curvature, producing stronger suppression than the parent's single fixed competitive surface permits.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when the evolving inhibition strength remains effectively constant over the trajectory, e.g. vanishing adaptation/crowding effect or regimes with P small enough that the modulation is negligible.
plan.promotion_reason: To express time- and trajectory-dependent inhibition strength within the closed vessel while preserving the existing states S and P, the inhibition constant itself must become a dynamical quantity; fixed parameters cannot encode history-dependent drift in the target mapping.
plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes a fixed product-inhibition constant even as product accumulates substantially, omitting plausible progressive changes in the enzyme's effective inhibitory sensitivity during the run.
plan.baseline_assumption: Enzyme concentration and catalytic properties remain constant.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Progressive alteration of effective product inhibition during turnover, such as slow conformational adaptation or crowding-driven strengthening of inhibitor binding as product accumulates.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's fixed-environment shortcut specifically in the already-present inhibition mechanism, rather than adding an unrelated side process. The parent says dP_dt is a fixed competitive function of S and P with one shared K_i, so once S and P are known the rate surface cannot change shape during the run. Under the same closed-vessel initial-condition protocol, vary only how far the trajectory proceeds in conversion (hence how large P becomes), while holding V_max, K_m, initial S, and the absence of side reactions fixed. Then the parent predicts one common inhibition curvature across early and late portions of all runs. A child with evolving effective K_i predicts a concrete contrast: little change at low P, but stronger late-time rate suppression when accumulated product exposure is substantial. This is a changed target mapping, not merely altered auxiliary trajectories, because dP_dt at the same observed (S,P) can differ once inhibition strength has drifted. The effect is scientifically admissible when product reaches at least order K_i or when long observation times allow slow adaptation to emerge; if all runs stay in low-conversion regimes, the refinement may be practically unidentifiable and the parent remains an adequate limit.

plan.baseline_assumption: Product inhibition is purely competitive and affects only the Michaelis denominator, not the catalytic capacity of the enzyme-product-substrate system.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Mixed product inhibition: accumulated product can bind a distinct or allosterically coupled enzyme form and reduce effective turnover in addition to competing with substrate binding.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the overly idealized inhibition form rather than add an unrelated process. The parent target mapping is single-phase in P: with V_max fixed, product can only act through the competitive denominator, giving one specific monotone decay shape of dP_dt as P rises along the closed-vessel trajectory. A single refit of the parent parameters cannot generally reproduce both early moderate-P behavior and stronger late high-P suppression across these conditions: increasing competitive strength enough to match late collapse also over-penalizes the rate when P is still modest, while adjusting V_max rescales all times without creating the extra P-dependent bending. plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the saturation of the revised K_i adaptation law to be effectively absent over the observed product range, so the adaptation reduces to the current linear-in-P decay form.
plan.gap_statement: The model assumes the product-driven evolution of the effective competitive inhibition constant is proportional to P at all product levels, implying unlimited growth in adaptation drive as product accumulates before the asymptote is reached.
plan.baseline_assumption: The effective inhibition-scale dynamics obey first-order decay with a product-proportional driving term -k_Ki_decay*P*(K_i-K_i_min).
plan.scientific_mechanism: Product-induced strengthening of competitive inhibition often reflects finite-site conformational or crowding adaptation, so the drive for further reduction in K_i should itself saturate as product occupancy/exposure becomes high.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the linear exposure assumption in the K_i state equation, not to add a wholly new process. The parent target mapping has a single-phase shortcut: for fixed V_max, K_m, K_icat, and k_Islow_relax, the scored rate changes with product through one instantaneous competitive term and one delayed suppression state, while the competitive-adaptation state K_i is driven by a linearly increasing function of P. Varying time along the standard closed-vessel trajectory changes P while initial conditions and enzyme conditions are held fixed. Under admissible conditions where product reaches moderate to high levels and K_i is still above K_i_min, the child would show a different dP_dt-versus-P curvature: early product rise can strengthen inhibition noticeably, but later increases in P produce diminishing additional change in K_i and therefore a partial flattening of the rate-law distortion. A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce both an initially strong adaptation response and a later saturation of that same adaptation drive if both are visible on the same observed trajectory, because its K_i dynamics remain proportional to P throughout. This affects the target mapping directly, not only an auxiliary state, since K_i enters the denominator of dP_dt. The contrast is limited when P never leaves the low-product regime or when K_i is already near K_i_min, in which case the refinement may be practically unidentifiable.

response_change.parent_relation: The target rate decreases with product through an instantaneous competitive factor P/K_i and a single delayed noncompetitive suppression load I_slow, so product inhibition enters as one smooth phase of slowing tied directly to P and one linear relaxation toward P.
response_change.child_relation: Retain the same inhibited Michaelis structure but relax the assumption that the competitive product-inhibition strength adapts linearly with cumulative product exposure; instead make that adaptation saturate with product so the target shows an early strong curvature change that later plateaus in its sensitivity to further product accumulation.
response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories with the same initial substrate and enzyme settings, the child predicts that dP_dt versus P can bend more sharply at intermediate product levels and then partially stabilize because competitive inhibition strengthening saturates, whereas the parent keeps progressively changing inhibition strength in a single exponential-like fashion.

contract.activation_condition: Observable when product rises to a scale comparable to the adaptation-driving range so that K_i has moved appreciably away from its initial value but not yet fully to K_i_min; if product stays very low or K_i remains near constant, the contrast is weak.
contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate product accumulation already reveals departure from a single-phase decline in competitive inhibition scale; in holdout, later-time higher-product segments extend this into a visible plateau of K_i evolution and corresponding dP_dt curvature change.
contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the saturation of the revised K_i adaptation law to be effectively absent over the observed product range, so the adaptation reduces to the current linear-in-P decay form.
contract.domain_mechanism: finite-capacity product-driven adaptation of competitive inhibition strength
contract.scientific_mechanism: Product-induced strengthening of competitive inhibition often reflects finite-site conformational or crowding adaptation, so the drive for further reduction in K_i should itself saturate as product occupancy/exposure becomes high.
contract.difficulty_rationale: This embedding is harder than a coefficient-only correction because it changes the shape of the product-to-K_i drive from unbounded linear growth to a finite-capacity saturating response, which in turn changes the trajectory-level curvature of the scored dP_dt mapping through K_i rather than merely rescaling an existing term.
contract.assumption_before: Competitive inhibition-scale adaptation is driven proportionally by product at all product levels.
contract.assumption_after: Competitive inhibition-scale adaptation is driven by product with finite-capacity saturation at high product burden.
contract.parent_reduction: As K_P_sat becomes much larger than observed P, the saturating drive behaves approximately linearly in P over the sampled trajectory after absorbing the scale into k_Ki_decay.
contract.observable_signature: With fixed initial substrate and enzyme settings, plotting dP_dt against P along the trajectory shows stronger intermediate bending followed by partial stabilization once product reaches the adaptation-driving range, because K_i evolution slows despite further product accumulation; the parent instead maintains a single-phase increase in adaptation drive proportional to P.
contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce both an initially strong adaptation response and a later saturation of that same adaptation drive when both regimes are visible on one observed trajectory, because its K_i dynamics remain proportional to P throughout. Refitting V_max, K_m, K_icat, k_Ki_decay, or k_Islow_relax can shift rate scale or timing but cannot create the finite-capacity plateau in product-driven K_i evolution that directly feeds back into the scored dP_dt mapping.

range_suggestions.K_P_sat: positive and on the product concentration scale; values comparable to reachable P produce visible saturation of K_i adaptation, while much larger values make the revised law approach the parent over the observed trajectory
